title: Edge buffer calibration — weekly sprint log (Mar 5 2029)
content:
Context: sprint 12 focused on reducing tail latency caused by cold KV-cache misses on edge regions. This doc captures the week’s experiments, a small incident postmortem, updated heuristics we prototyped, and owner action items for next sprint.

Date: 2029-03-05
Attendees: Priya Nair, Liam O'Connor, Maya Patel, Diego Romero, Hannah Lee, Arjun Gupta (notes)

High-level summary:
- Experimented with an occupancy-based buffer allocator (OB-allocator) that holds a soft reservation per zone keyed by recent token-distribution heatmap. Goal: keep hot prefixes primed without blowing buffer budget.
- Observed 18% reduction in 95th-token latency in ap-south-edge during synthetic chat surge (baseline: 210ms 95p -> 172ms). CPU/GPU mem overhead ~+4% on allocator bookkeeping.
- One short incident on 2029-03-04 (09:12–09:38 UTC): allocation loop slowed due to a bad eviction threshold regression (PR 3169). Fallback triggered to conservative LRU and service restored; no customer-visible errors but elevated latencies recorded.

Telemetry & metrics we care about (this week’s snapshots):
- Global buffer hit rate (prefix KV): 0.62 -> target 0.7 over next 3 sprints
- Edge ap-south 95th-token latency: 210ms -> 172ms (experiment run)
- Avg per-request memory delta with OB-allocator: +120MB (mostly bookkeeping)
- Prewarm coverage (requests that benefited from warm cache): 34% -> 44% in test window

Detailed notes:
1) OB-allocator prototype results
   - Approach: maintain lightweight sliding-window occupancy histograms per shard (5m window), compute soft reservation=percentile(occupancy, 80) * safety_factor. Implemented in allocator v0.3.
   - Pros: better locality for high-volume prefixes, avoids global thrashing during multi-tenant spikes.
   - Cons: bookkeeping CPU increased; worst-case reservation can starve new cold prefixes if safety_factor too high.
   - Next: tune safety_factor per-region and add a short randomized admission token to avoid pathological starvation. Owner: Liam. Due: 2029-03-12.

2) Incident 2029-03-04 postmortem (short)
   - Trigger: a threshold change in PR 3169 (removed a guard for negative deltas under certain eviction patterns).
   - Detection: internal alert CPU spike + allocator backlog metric > 3x baseline.
   - Mitigation: automated rollback via canary policy executed at 09:18 UTC; full rollback 09:28. Root cause fix: restore guard and add unit + integration test to cover negative-delta branch. Owners: Diego (fix), Hannah (tests). Deployed: 2029-03-05.

3) Cross-region orchestration test (warm handoff)
   - Ran a controlled failover (LAX -> FRA) for low-priority traffic to measure handoff cost with OB-allocator. Cold miss penalty measured: extra 360ms tail tokens. Hypothesis: prewarm handshake needed for fast failover.
   - Action: add a lightweight prefix-summary exchange during handoff (only top-100 prefixes) — prototype in branch perf/edge-handoff. Owner: Arjun. Due: 2029-03-19.

4) Cost vs latency tradeoff analysis
   - Simulation: increasing prewarm budget by 15% reduces 95p by ~12% but increases infra mem footprint by ~9% which maps to ~6% cost rise for edge instances.
   - Recommendation: use dynamic prewarm scaling tied to business-priority band (low/med/high) with nightly reclaiming for non-peak windows. Product alignment needed for bands. Owner: Priya + Maya to coordinate with product-hosted-api. Due: 2029-03-15.

Open experiments (running):
- Randomized admission token to prevent starvation (Liam) — early results show elimination of 2 pathological cases but increases variance slightly.
- Prefix-summary handshake compression (Arjun) — testing compression ratio tradeoffs for limited bandwidth links.

Action items & owners:
- Liam O'Connor: tune safety_factor per-region, run A/B in eu-west and ap-south. Due 2029-03-12.
- Diego Romero: finalize regression test and backfill unit tests for eviction edge cases, merge PR. Done 2029-03-05.
- Hannah Lee: add integration scenario to SRE synthetic harness for allocator backlog detection. Due 2029-03-12.
- Arjun Gupta: prototype top-100 prefix handshake + compression and validate handoff latency. Due 2029-03-19.
- Priya Nair & Maya Patel: draft proposal for dynamic prewarm policy mapped to product priority bands and cost guardrails. Draft due 2029-03-15.

Risks & open questions:
- If occupancy histograms drift due to diurnal traffic shifts, we could oscillate between over-reserving and under-provisioning. Need a damping mechanism.
- Edge regions with limited memory (some APAC microregions) may not tolerate OB-allocator overhead; we need per-region fallbacks.
- Product buy-in for dynamic prewarm bands is required before rollout; lack of alignment increases risk of over-provisioning edge spend.

Notes to self / quick wins:
- Add an emergency throttle on safety_factor scaling (hard cap) to avoid simultaneous region-wide overcommit.
- Add a short Slack runbook for on-call to quickly trigger allocator rollback (one-click) — Diego to add.

Appendix (links):
- Playbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Edge+Buffer+Calibration+Playbook
- Recent PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3169 (incident), /pull/3178 (allocator v0.3)
